headline: Australia stun Turkey 2-0 in World Cup opener
summary: The Socceroos secure a dominant victory, spoiling Turkey's return to the World Cup stage after 24 years.
details: Australia defeated Turkey 2-0 in their Group D opener on Saturday, with goals from Nestory Irankunda and Connor Metcalfe.
The first goal came in the 27th minute when Irankunda controlled a ball over the top, beat a defender, and finished inside the near post.
Australia's defense remained resolute throughout the match, repelling all of Turkey's attacks to maintain a clean sheet.
Connor Metcalfe doubled the lead in the 75th minute, collecting the ball around 20 yards out and sweeping it home.
The victory puts Australia second in the group, trailing only the United States, who defeated Paraguay 4-1 on Friday.
caption:
Australia spoils Turkey's long-awaited return to the World Cup stage with a clinical 2-0 win!

Australia defeated Turkey 2-0 in their Group D opener on Saturday, with goals from Nestory Irankunda and Connor Metcalfe.

The first goal came in the 27th minute when Irankunda controlled a ball over the top, beat a defender, and finished inside the near post.

Australia's defense remained resolute throughout the match, repelling all of Turkey's attacks to maintain a clean sheet.

Connor Metcalfe doubled the lead in the 75th minute, collecting the ball around 20 yards out and sweeping it home.

The victory puts Australia second in the group, trailing only the United States, who defeated Paraguay 4-1 on Friday.

headline_marked: Measles death toll [[rises to 69]] after child dies in Sylhet
headline: Measles death toll rises to 69 after child dies in Sylhet
summary: Health experts warn of the disease's return with alarming force, urging immediate vaccination to prevent severe complications and further deaths.
details: A child has died with measles symptoms in Sylhet, bringing the total death toll from the illness to 69. The disease, once thought to be fading, is spreading across several countries, including Bangladesh.
Measles is highly contagious and spreads easily through coughing or sneezing, with droplets that can linger in the air or on surfaces. This makes transmission difficult to avoid in crowded areas.

While many children recover with proper care, delays in seeking medical attention can lead to severe complications. These include breathing difficulties, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, and swelling of the brain.
Health authorities emphasize that vaccination is the strongest defense against the illness. The vaccine offers excellent protection and has saved millions of lives worldwide.
Experts highlight the importance of community-wide protection, known as herd immunity. When most people are immune, the virus struggles to find new hosts and loses its ability to spread.
This collective shield not only protects those who are vaccinated but also safeguards vulnerable children who are too young to receive the vaccine.
caption:
Measles death toll rises to 69 after another child dies in Sylhet. A disease once thought to be fading is returning with alarming force.

A child has died with measles symptoms in Sylhet, bringing the total death toll from the illness to 69. The disease, once thought to be fading, is spreading across several countries, including Bangladesh.

Measles is highly contagious and spreads easily through coughing or sneezing, with droplets that can linger in the air or on surfaces. This makes transmission difficult to avoid in crowded areas.

While many children recover with proper care, delays in seeking medical attention can lead to severe complications. These include breathing difficulties, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, and swelling of the brain.

Health authorities emphasize that vaccination is the strongest defense against the illness. The vaccine offers excellent protection and has saved millions of lives worldwide.

Experts highlight the importance of community-wide protection, known as herd immunity. When most people are immune, the virus struggles to find new hosts and loses its ability to spread.

This collective shield not only protects those who are vaccinated but also safeguards vulnerable children who are too young to receive the vaccine.
